title: Unlocking a New Rust Programming Experience: Fast and Slow Thinking with LLMs to Conquer Undefined Behaviors
problem: Eliminating Undefined Behaviors (UBs) in Rust programs written with the 'unsafe' tag; manual UB detection requires deep understanding of Rust safety rules and strong typing, which is laborious and error-prone.
motivation: Rust's 'unsafe' tag provides flexibility and low-level control but introduces UBs that reduce memory safety; traditional manual analysis is labor-intensive and depends on developer expertise.
method: RustBrain uses a large language model (LLM—a machine learning system trained on vast text) to find and fix undefined behaviors in Rust 'unsafe' code. It employs two complementary thinking modes inspired by cognitive science: a 'fast thinking' phase that quickly identifies code patterns and proposes fixes, and a 'slow thinking' phase that carefully breaks down those proposals, verifies whether they work, and generalizes them (adapts them to similar patterns). A feedback loop connects verification and generalization results back to generation, so each cycle improves the system's future proposals.
key_novelty: It applies dual-process thinking (a cognitive science framework where the mind uses both quick intuition and careful deliberation) through a large language model to identify and fix undefined behaviors in Rust code.
contributions: RustBrain LLM framework for automated UB minimization in Rust projects
Fast-Slow thinking architecture with feature extraction and abstract verification
Feedback mechanism for dynamic solution adjustment and generalization
94.3% pass rate and 80.4% execution rate on Miri dataset

metrics.accuracy: 94.3% pass rate; 80.4% execution rate on Miri dataset

primary_theme: LLM-based Rust UB elimination via dual-process thinking
